sentences.text: 1  ORDER Shri Prateek Rusia, learned counsel for the respondent No.2, submits that in this case as per calculation sheet Annx.R2/1, compensation has been paid in accordance with the provisions contained in the Right to Fair Compensation & Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as the Act of 2013 for short).

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation & Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Drawing attention to page 37, annexed with the petition, it is submitted that some amount was paid on 22.11.2014 and the difference of amount calculated in terms of the provisions contained in the Act of 2013, were paid on 20.01.2016.

Thus, drawing attention to Annx.P/7, it is submitted that amounts have been paid pursuance to and the calculation to be made in terms of the provisions contained in the Act of 2013 and petitioner has any grievance, then his remedy is under Section 64 of the Act of 2013.

In view of such facts, though Shri Atulanand Awasthy, Senior Advocate, disputes certain facts and submits that in the earlier round of litigation, High Court in Writ Petition No.2163/2015, copy enclosed as Annx.P/4(a), vide order dated 25.02.2015, had disposed of the petition, with a direction to the Land Acquisition Officer to redetermine the compensation as per the provisions of the Act of 2013, within a period of six months from the date of receipt of certified copy of the order passed today.
Therefore, he submits that now there is no scope for further reference etc.

It is evident from the record that Annx.R2/1, is though undated but Annx.P/7, makes it abundantly clear that in terms of the order dated 25.02.2015, passed in Writ Petition No.2163/2015, authorities have already made a recalculation, as is evident from third row in which name of the petitioner appears and in Column No.17, difference between the amount earlier calculated and which is payable under the Act of 2013,
is mentioned and thereafter, in Column 18, total sum of Rs.35,88,000/- (Rupees Thirty Five Lacs and Eighty Eight Thousand) is mentioned as the amount payable towards the compensation, out of which the amount already paid, was deducted and it is mentioned that after deduction of income tax, a sum of Rs.10,86,750/- (Rupees Ten Lacs, Eighty Six Thousand, Seven Hundred and Fifty), is payable which appears from Annx.P/7 to have been paid on 20.01.2016.

In view of such facts, if petitioner has any dispute, then statutory provisions contained in Section 64 of the Act of 2013,
cannot be given a go bye.

Let petitioner will be free to approach the authority by filing a reference, inasmuch as, petitioner has refused the offer of this Court to grant interest for the delayed period in making the calculation as per the provisions contained in the Act of 2013, and if, such reference is made within thirty days from today, then the authority shall consider and decide the same within a further period of 90 days.
This Court has not expressed any opinion in regard to the difference to be made by the petitioner.
In above terms, petition is disposed of.
(VIVEK AGARWAL) JUDGE A.Praj.
